<!-- Third-party code from the original study, kept verbatim. It needs the raw human files
     Player_one.csv, Player_two.csv and Demographic.csv (not redistributed here; see data/README.md)
     in the working directory. -->

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidybayes)
library(rstan)
library(ggplot2)
library(shinystan)
library(loo)
library(patchwork)
library(HDInterval)

mytheme <-
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold",
      size = (25),
      colour = "steelblue4"
    ),
    axis.title = element_text(
      size = (25),
      colour = "steelblue4",
      face = "bold"
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "cornflowerblue", size = (25)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(vjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 25),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 25),
    legend.text = element_text(size=25),
    legend.key.size = unit(2, 'cm')
  )

cb1 <- c("#999999", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7")

log_to_prob <- function(logit){
  return(1 / (1 + exp(-logit)))
}

prob_to_log <- function(p){
  return(log(p / (1 - p)))
}

softmax_function <- function(values) {
  exp_values <- exp(values)
  p_values <- exp_values / sum(exp_values)
  return(p_values)
}
```

## Load in the datasets 

```{r}
Player_one <- read.csv("Player_one.csv") %>%
  select(-X)
Player_two <- read.csv("Player_two.csv") %>%
  select(-X)
Demographics <- read.csv("Demographic.csv") %>%
  select(-X)
```

## A little extra tidying 

Perform a little bit of extra tidying for Player one.

```{r}
Player_one <- Player_one %>%
  mutate(Dishonesty_value = Answer - Advice,
         Dishonesty_value_abs = abs(Answer - Advice),
         Advice_dishonesty = ifelse(Dishonesty_value_abs != 0, 1, 0),
         Dishonesty_magnitude = Dishonesty_value_abs / 20,
         Condition_recoded = case_when(
           Condition == "Cooperative" ~ 1,
           Condition == "Competitive" ~ 2,
           Condition == "Neutral" ~ 3 
         ),
         Condition_recoded = factor(Condition_recoded),
         Second_Block = ifelse(Question > 10, 1, 0),
         participant_id = match(participant_id, unique(participant_id)),
         participant_id = factor(participant_id))
```

Perform a little bit of extra tidying for Player two. 

```{r}
Player_two <- Player_two %>%
  mutate(Answer_difference = (Second_answer - First_answer),
         Information_difference = Social_info - First_answer,
         Condition_recoded = case_when(
           Condition == "Cooperative" ~ 1,
           Condition == "Competitive" ~ 2,
           Condition == "Neutral" ~ 3
         ),
         Condition_recoded = factor(Condition_recoded),
         Second_Block = ifelse(Question > 10, 1, 0),
         Spied = ifelse(Type == "Spied", 1, 0),
         Advice = ifelse(Type == "Advice", 1, 0),
         Type = ifelse(is.na(Type), "None", Type), # If participants chose to see no information in block 2
         participant_id = match(participant_id, unique(participant_id)),
         participant_id = factor(participant_id)) 

table(Player_two$Spied, Player_two$Type)
table(Player_two$Advice, Player_two$Type)
```

Divide by 20 to get the condition number, as there are 20 rows of data per participant. 

```{r}
table(Player_two$Condition) / 20
table(Player_one$Condition) / 20
```

Calculate the correct answer for each question

```{r}
Correct_answers <- Player_one %>%
  mutate(Correct_answer = Blue - Yellow) %>%
  select(Group, Question, Correct_answer)

Player_two <- left_join(Player_two, Correct_answers)
```

### Model one

Reminder of the conditions (stored in Condition_recoded):

1 = Cooperative
2 = Competitive
3 = Neutral

```{r}
A_stan <- Player_one %>%
  select(Condition_recoded, participant_id, Advice_dishonesty) %>%
  compose_data(
    Condition = Condition_recoded,
    Dishonest_advice = Advice_dishonesty,
    ppt = participant_id,
  )
```

```{stan output.var="A_Model_1"}
data {
  int<lower=1> n;
  int n_participant_id;
  int Dishonest_advice[n];
  int Condition[n];
  int ppt[n];  
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0, upper=50> sigma_participant;
  vector[3] b_condition;
  vector[n_participant_id] z_a;
  real a_bar;
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[n_participant_id] a;
  a = a_bar + sigma_participant * z_a;

}

model {
  for (i in 1:n) {
    Dishonest_advice[i] ~ bernoulli_logit(a[ppt[i]] + b_condition[Condition[i]]);
  }
  z_a ~ normal(0, 1);
  a_bar ~ normal(0, 0.5);
  sigma_participant ~ exponential(1); 
  b_condition ~ normal(0, 0.5);
}
```

```{r}
Model_1A <- sampling(A_Model_1, iter = 13000, warmup = 3000, chains = 4, cores = 4, data = A_stan)
Model_1A

# summary <- summary(Model_1A)
# rhat <- summary$summary[, "Rhat"]
# max(rhat)

#launch_shinystan(Model_1A)
```
## Generating predictions 

```{r}
# Model with participant effect
Model_A1 <- extract(Model_1A)
```

Examine the participant effect

a = a_bar + sigma_participant * z_a;

```{r}
a_bar <- Model_A1$a_bar
sigma <- Model_A1$sigma_participant
z_a <- Model_A1$z_a %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  colMeans() %>%
  unname()

a_bar %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  summarise("M" = round(mean(.),2), "Upper 95%" = rethinking::PI(., prob = 0.95)[2], "Lower 95%" = rethinking::PI(., prob = 0.95)[1])

sigma %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  summarise("M" = round(mean(.),2), "Upper 95%" = rethinking::PI(., prob = 0.95)[2], "Lower 95%" = rethinking::PI(., prob = 0.95)[1])

Participant_effect <- a_bar + sigma * mean(z_a)
Full_participant_effect <- a_bar + sigma * z_a
mean_participant <- mean(Full_participant_effect)

Plotting_data <- data.frame(
  Participant_effect = Participant_effect
)

## Generate N samples random draws from the distribution of participant effects

Plotting_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Participant_effect)) + 
  geom_density(fill = "#999999", col = "#999999") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_participant, lty = 2, col = "red", linewidth = 1.5) + 
  mytheme + 
  labs(x = "Participant effect") + 
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())

ggsave("Participant_effect.png", width = 12, height = 12, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
# N predictions of the probability of giving dishonest advice
Probability_predictions <- tibble(
  Cooperative = log_to_prob(a_bar + Cooperative),
  Competitive = log_to_prob(a_bar + Competitive),
  Neutral = log_to_prob(a_bar + Neutral),
)

Probability_predictions_long <- Probability_predictions %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Condition", values_to = "P") %>%
  mutate(Condition = as.factor(Condition))

Probability_predictions_long %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  summarise("M" = mean(P), "Upper 95%" = rethinking::PI(P, prob = 0.95)[2], "Lower 95%" = rethinking::PI(P, prob = 0.95)[1])
```

Contrasts

```{r}
tibble(
  Comp_Coop = Probability_predictions$Competitive - Probability_predictions$Cooperative,
  Comp_Neutral = Probability_predictions$Competitive - Probability_predictions$Neutral,
  Coop_Neutral = Probability_predictions$Cooperative - Probability_predictions$Neutral
) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Condition", values_to = "Contrast") %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  summarise("Mean" = round(mean(Contrast),2), "Upper 95%" = round(rethinking::PI(Contrast, prob = 0.95)[2],2), "Lower 95%" = round(rethinking::PI(Contrast, prob = 0.95)[1],2), "% Positive" = round((sum(Contrast > 0) / 40000) * 100,2))
```

### Model two

Reminder of the conditions:

1 = Cooperative
2 = Competitive
3 = Neutral

```{r}
B_stan <- Player_two %>%
  filter(Type != "None") %>%# Drop cases where they opted for no social information in part 2
  compose_data(y = Answer_difference,
               Info_type = Type,
               Condition = Condition_recoded,
               ppt = participant_id,
               Second_block = Second_Block,
               Advice = Advice,
               Spied = Spied)

table("Type" = B_stan$Type, "Advice" = B_stan$Advice)
```

Non centered parameterisation was necessary for this model to run.

```{stan output.var="B_Model_1"}
data {
  int<lower=1> n;
  vector[n] Answer_difference; 
  vector[n] Information_difference;
  int n_participant_id; 
  int Advice[n];
  int Second_block[n];
  int Condition[n];
  int ppt[n];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0,upper=5> sigma; 
  real<lower=0,upper=5> sigma_participant;
  vector[3] b_condition;
  real b_advice;
  real b_block;
  vector[n_participant_id] participant_effect;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[n] influence;
  vector[n] mu; 
  for(i in 1:n){
   influence[i] = b_condition[Condition[i]] * (1 + b_advice * Advice[i] + b_block * Second_block[i]) + participant_effect[ppt[i]];
   mu[i] =  influence[i] * Information_difference[i];
  }  
}
model {
  Answer_difference ~ normal(mu, sigma);
  sigma ~ exponential(1); 
  b_advice ~ normal(0,0.5);
  b_block ~ normal(0,0.5);
  b_condition ~ normal(0,0.5);
  participant_effect ~ normal(0, sigma_participant);
  sigma_participant ~ exponential(1);
}
```

```{r}
ModelB_1 <- sampling(B_Model_1, iter = 5000, warmup = 1500, chains = 4, cores = 4, data = B_stan)
ModelB_1
```

## Investigating the increased influence in block 2

If the answer difference and information difference are both 0, you get NaN.

You get Inf if the participant changed by something, despite their first guess matching the social information. 

So, both these cases are excluded. 

```{r}
Participant_trust <- Player_two %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
    mutate(Advice = sum(Second_Block == 1 & Type == "Advice"),
         Spying = sum(Second_Block == 1 & Type == "Spied"),
         No_info = sum(Second_Block == 1 & Type == "None")) %>%
  mutate(Prop_influence = Answer_difference / Information_difference,
         Prop_influence = ifelse(is.na(Prop_influence), 5000, Prop_influence)) %>% # For some reason, the code was dropping the NaN values too early. So we set them to a number then reassign to NA to drop after social info choice calculations
  filter(Prop_influence != Inf, Prop_influence != -Inf, Second_Block == 0) %>% # Exclude the second block estimate 
  mutate(Prop_influence = ifelse(Prop_influence == 5000, NA, Prop_influence)) %>%
  summarise(mean_influence = mean(Prop_influence, na.rm = T), Advice = mean(Advice), Spying = mean(Spying), `No Information` = mean(No_info), Condition = Condition) %>%
  distinct()
```

```{r}
Participant_trust %>%
  pivot_longer(Advice:`No Information`, names_to = "Choice", values_to = "Num_chosen") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Num_chosen, y = mean_influence, fill = Choice)) +
  geom_point(col = "#999999") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", col = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#999999", "#56B4E9", "#E69F00")) +
  labs(y = "Social influence (block 1)", x = "Number chosen (block 2)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0,5,10)) + 
  mytheme + 
  facet_grid(~Choice) +

ggsave("Social_influence_by_condition.png", width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```


```{r}
B_stan_3 <- B_stan_3 %>%
  compose_data(Info_choice = Info_choice,
               ppt = factor(participant_id),
               Condition = Condition_recoded)
```

1 = Choosing advice
2 = Choosing to spy
3 = Choosing no information

Conditions

1 = Coop
2 = Comp
3 = Neutral

Put the pivot onto the most common choice (spying), to help chain efficiency. 

```{stan output.var="B_model_2"}
data {
  int<lower=1> n;   // number of observations
  int n_participant_id;
  int Info_choice[n]; // outcome
  int Condition[n];
  int ppt[n];  
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma_participant;
  vector[3] b_condition1;
  vector[3] b_condition3;
  vector[n_participant_id] z_a1;
  vector[n_participant_id] z_a2;
  vector[n_participant_id] z_a3;
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[n_participant_id] a1;
  vector[n_participant_id] a2;
  vector[n_participant_id] a3;
  
  a1 = sigma_participant * z_a1;
  a2 = sigma_participant * z_a2;
  a3 = sigma_participant * z_a3;

}

model {
  vector[n] p;
  vector[3] s;
  for(i in 1:n){
    s[1] = a1[ppt[i]] + b_condition1[Condition[i]]; // Selecting advice
    s[2] = a2[ppt[i]];  // Selecting spying
    s[3] = a3[ppt[i]] + b_condition3[Condition[i]]; // Selecting no information
    
    Info_choice[i] ~ categorical(softmax(s));
  }

  // Priors
  z_a1 ~ normal(0, 2);
  z_a2 ~ normal(0, 2);
  z_a3 ~ normal(0, 2);
  sigma_participant ~ exponential(1);
  b_condition1 ~ normal(0, 2);
  b_condition3 ~ normal(0, 2);
}
```

```{r}
ModelB_2 <- sampling(B_model_2, iter = 5000, warmup = 1500, chains = 4, cores = 4, data = B_stan_3, control=list(adapt_delta=0.99))
```

### Model predictions from B_2

First, we generate predictions for S across the two conditions we model.

In each case, we calculate the average participant effect for each choice, based on the means of the parameters used to compute it.

```{r}
Model_2B <- extract(ModelB_2)
a1_mean <- mean(Model_2B$sigma_participant) * mean(Model_2B$z_a1)
a2_mean <- mean(Model_2B$sigma_participant) * mean(Model_2B$z_a2)
a3_mean <- mean(Model_2B$sigma_participant) * mean(Model_2B$z_a3)
  
Advice_coop <- a1_mean + Model_2B$b_condition1[,1]
Advice_comp <- a1_mean + Model_2B$b_condition1[,2]
Advice_neutral <- a1_mean + Model_2B$b_condition1[,3]

Spied_coop <- a2_mean
Spied_comp <- a2_mean
Spied_neutral <- a2_mean

None_coop <- a3_mean + Model_2B$b_condition3[,1]
None_comp <- a3_mean + Model_2B$b_condition3[,2]
None_neutral <- a3_mean + Model_2B$b_condition3[,3]

Coop_P <- sapply(1:14000, function(i)
  softmax_function(c(Advice_coop[i], Spied_coop, None_coop[i])))

Comp_P <- sapply(1:14000, function(i)
  softmax_function(c(Advice_comp[i], Spied_comp, None_comp[i])))

Neutral_P <- sapply(1:14000, function(i)
  softmax_function(c(Advice_neutral[i], Spied_neutral, None_neutral[i])))
```

### Interaction with condition for model two SI ###

Reminder of the conditions:

1 = Cooperative
2 = Competitive
3 = Neutral

```{r}
B_stan <- Player_two %>%
  filter(Type != "None") %>%# Drop cases where they opted for no social information in part 2
  compose_data(y = Answer_difference,
               Info_type = Type,
               Condition = Condition_recoded,
               ppt = participant_id,
               Second_block = Second_Block,
               Advice = Advice,
               Spied = Spied)

table("Type" = B_stan$Type, "Advice" = B_stan$Advice)
```

This model is the same as B_model_2, except an additional interaction is added with condition. 

```{stan output.var="B_Model_3"}
data {
  int<lower=1> n;
  vector[n] Answer_difference; 
  vector[n] Information_difference;
  int n_participant_id; 
  int Advice[n];
  int Second_block[n];
  int Condition[n];
  int ppt[n];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0,upper=5> sigma; 
  real<lower=0,upper=5> sigma_participant;
  vector[3] b_condition;
  vector[3] b_advice;
  real b_block;
  vector[n_participant_id] participant_effect;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[n] influence;
  vector[n] mu; 
  for(i in 1:n){
   influence[i] = b_condition[Condition[i]] * (1 + b_advice[Condition[i]] * Advice[i] + b_block * Second_block[i]) + participant_effect[ppt[i]];
   mu[i] =  influence[i] * Information_difference[i];
  }  
}
model {
  Answer_difference ~ normal(mu, sigma);
  sigma ~ exponential(1); 
  b_advice ~ normal(0,0.5);
  b_block ~ normal(0,0.5);
  b_condition ~ normal(0,0.5);
  participant_effect ~ normal(0, sigma_participant);
  sigma_participant ~ exponential(1);
}
```

```{r}
ModelB_3 <- sampling(B_Model_3, iter = 5000, warmup = 1500, chains = 4, cores = 4, data = B_stan)
ModelB_3
```


```{stan output.var="Count_model"}
data {
  int<lower=1> n;
  vector[n] y; 
  int Combination[n];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0,upper=5> sigma; 
  vector[9] b_combination;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[n] mu; 
  for(i in 1:n){
   mu[i] =  b_combination[Combination[i]];
  }  
}
model {
  y ~ normal(mu, sigma);
  sigma ~ exponential(1); 
  b_combination ~ normal(10,2);
}
```
```{r}
Model_count <- sampling(Count_model, iter = 5000, warmup = 1500, chains = 4, cores = 4, data = count_stan)
Model_count 
```
```{r}
Count_model_samples <- extract(Model_count)
```
Contrasts for cooperative condition 

```{r}
# Player 1 vs Player 2 no info
mean_qi(Count_model_samples$b_combination[,1] - Count_model_samples$b_combination[,2])

# Player 1 vs Player 2 info
mean_qi(Count_model_samples$b_combination[,1] - Count_model_samples$b_combination[,3])

# Player 2 no info vs Player 2 info
mean_qi(Count_model_samples$b_combination[,2] - Count_model_samples$b_combination[,3])
```

Additional contrasts between conditions for player two first and player two second. Is there any difference in improvement between conditions?

```{r}
Cooperative_contrast <- Count_model_samples$b_combination[,2] - Count_model_samples$b_combination[,3]
Neutral_contrast <- Count_model_samples$b_combination[,5] - Count_model_samples$b_combination[,6]
Competitive_contrast <- Count_model_samples$b_combination[,8] - Count_model_samples$b_combination[,9]

mean_qi(Cooperative_contrast - Neutral_contrast)
mean_qi(Cooperative_contrast - Competitive_contrast)
mean_qi(Neutral_contrast - Competitive_contrast)
```
